title: scripts/apply-artifact.mjs: refuse to copy a shipped ticket's artifact over a live file that changed since the implementer last saw it
question: The ticket pipeline's own README (scripts/tickets/README.md, step 6) says a shipped artifact is copied into the repository by hand: "Copy it in yourself, run the FULL suite, and only then close the item... the runner never writes into the repository." That copy is a plain overwrite of whatever is currently at the file's path, with no check that the path still holds what the implementer was shown when it wrote the diff. On 2026-09-28 this happened for real: an operator's copy of a shipped src/board/run-item.mjs artifact silently overwrote a DIFFERENT, concurrent Claude Code session's own in-progress edit to that same file, in this same shared, non-worktree-isolated checkout -- the other session had already committed by then, and its commit captured the clobbered file instead of its own work, costing it a wasted commit-and-reset cycle to recover. The pipeline itself never collided (every ticket run works in its own isolated board/worktree); the collision was entirely in the manual, ungated "copy it in yourself" step. Every implementer prompt already records, verbatim, the exact file contents it was shown at revision 1 ("Current contents of <path>:" in outputs/open-items/<key>/implementer-prompt-<key>-rev1.txt) -- what is the smallest tool that uses that already-recorded baseline to refuse an apply when the live file no longer matches it, rather than silently overwriting?
goal:
Create scripts/apply-artifact.mjs, a new standalone CLI script (it must run as `node scripts/apply-artifact.mjs --key <key>` from the repository root, matching scripts/open-items-run.mjs's own invocation style). It must export ONE function for testing, `checkApply({ key, outputsDir, repoRoot })`, and a thin CLI wrapper at the bottom that calls it and sets the process exit code (module-style: guard the CLI block with `if (import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\``) so importing the module for tests never runs the CLI).

`checkApply({ key, outputsDir, repoRoot })` (all three required; `outputsDir` defaults to `join(repoRoot, "outputs", "open-items", key)` when omitted):

1. Read `<outputsDir>/run.json`. Its `artifact.copied_to` field is the absolute path to the shipped bytes. The shipped-artifact directory is `join(outputsDir, "artifact")` -- you already know this exactly, from the SAME `outputsDir` this function was given; do not rediscover it by searching `copied_to` for a `/artifact/` substring, since the ticket's own ROOT PATH can itself legitimately contain the literal text "artifact" (e.g. a repo checked out under a directory named `.../my-artifact-repo/...`), which would make a generic substring search find the wrong occurrence and extract the wrong path. Instead: normalize both to absolute form and derive the ticket's own `path` as whatever remains of `copied_to` after that exact `join(outputsDir, "artifact")` prefix (plus its trailing separator). If `copied_to` does not start with that exact prefix, that is itself a `{ safe: false, reason: "shipped artifact path is not under this ticket's own artifact directory" }` result, not a generic parse failure. If `run.json` is missing or has no `artifact.copied_to`, return `{ safe: false, reason: "no shipped artifact recorded for this key" }` -- never throw for a normal, checkable precondition failure; only throw for a truly unexpected filesystem error.
2. Read `<outputsDir>/implementer-prompt-<key>-rev1.txt` (rev1 specifically, always -- it is the only revision whose artifact section shows the true pre-ticket file, since revision 2+ shows the PRIOR FAILED revision instead). If this file is missing, return `{ safe: false, reason: "no rev1 implementer prompt found; cannot recover the pre-ticket baseline" }`.
3. Within that prompt text, find the line `Current contents of <path>:` (the literal ticket path from step 1, exactly, with a trailing colon) followed by two newlines, and take everything from there up to but not including the next line that is exactly `[tests]` (a template section marker that always follows). That slice, with exactly one trailing newline removed if present (the template inserts `${current}` followed immediately by two newlines before the next section), is the baseline. If the `Current contents of <path>:` line is not found at all, return `{ safe: false, reason: "rev1 prompt does not show 'Current contents of <path>:'; cannot recover a baseline" }`.
4. Read the LIVE file at `join(repoRoot, path)` if it exists, else treat its content as `""` (matching how the implementer prompt itself represents an absent file per src/board/run-item.mjs's `existsSync(...) ? readFileSync(...) : ""`).
5. Compare the baseline (step 3) to the live content (step 4) byte for byte. Equal: return `{ safe: true, path, reason: null }`. Different: return `{ safe: false, path, reason: "live file differs from what the implementer was shown; something else changed it since this ticket started", baseline, live }` (include both full strings so a caller can diff them).

CLI wrapper: parse `--key <key>` (required; usage + exit 2 if missing) and an optional `--apply` flag. Always call `checkApply({ key, repoRoot: process.cwd() })` and print `path`/`reason` plainly. Without `--apply`: print `SAFE to apply` or `REFUSED: <reason>` and exit 0 if safe, 1 if not -- never writes anything. With `--apply`: if safe, copy `outputs/open-items/<key>/artifact/<path>` over `<path>` (creating parent directories as needed) and print `applied <path>`, exit 0; if not safe, print `REFUSED: <reason>` to stderr, write nothing, and exit 1.

The acceptance command runs the project's test files (excluding one known-flaky, unrelated sibling test), including the new tests/apply-artifact-guard.test.mjs; every included test must stay green.
constraints: ES module syntax; Node built-ins only; no new dependencies
one file changes: scripts/apply-artifact.mjs (a new file; nothing else in the repository is edited)
checkApply never writes to disk under any circumstances; only the CLI's --apply path writes, and only when checkApply returned safe:true
the baseline always comes from implementer-prompt-<key>-rev1.txt specifically, never a later revision's prompt
a missing run.json, missing rev1 prompt, or unparseable baseline is a checkable {safe:false, reason} result, never an uncaught exception
forbidden: do not elect a vendor as judge
do not edit any test file
do not edit src/, bin/, .agents/, docs/, or any file other than scripts/apply-artifact.mjs
do not modify scripts/open-items-run.mjs or the README to call this automatically; wiring it into the normal flow is a separate, later change
